passage.text: We usually think of mistakes as bad things.
passage.reading: wiː ˈjuːʒuəli ˈθɪŋk əv mɪˈsteɪks əz ˈbæd ˈθɪŋz.

passage.text: But some of the most important discoveries in history happened by accident.
passage.reading: bʌt sʌm əv ðə ˈmoʊst ɪmˈpɔːrtənt dɪˈskʌvəriz ɪn ˈhɪstəri ˈhæpənd baɪ ˈæksɪdənt.

passage.text: Here are three accidental discoveries that changed the world.
passage.reading: ˈhɪr ər ˈθriː ˌæksɪˈdɛntəl dɪˈskʌvəriz ðæt ˈtʃeɪndʒd ðə ˈwɜːrld.

passage.text: In 1928, a British scientist named Alexander Fleming went on vacation and left some dishes of bacteria in his laboratory.
passage.reading: ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈtwɛnti ˈeɪt, ə ˈbrɪtɪʃ ˈsaɪəntɪst ˈneɪmd ˌælɪɡˈzændər ˈflɛmɪŋ ˈwɛnt ɑːn veɪˈkeɪʃən ənd ˈlɛft sʌm ˈdɪʃɪz əv bækˈtɪriə ɪn hɪz ˈlæbrətɔːri.

passage.text: When he came back, he noticed that mold was growing on one of the dishes.
passage.reading: wɛn hiː ˈkeɪm ˈbæk, hiː ˈnoʊtɪst ðæt ˈmoʊld wʌz ˈɡroʊɪŋ ɑːn ˈwʌn əv ðə ˈdɪʃɪz.

passage.text: Around the mold, there were no bacteria.
passage.reading: əˈraʊnd ðə ˈmoʊld, ðɛr wɜːr ˈnoʊ bækˈtɪriə.

passage.text: This mold led to penicillin, a medicine that has saved millions of lives.
passage.reading: ðɪs ˈmoʊld ˈlɛd tə ˌpɛnɪˈsɪlɪn, ə ˈmɛdəsən ðæt hæz ˈseɪvd ˈmɪljənz əv ˈlɪvz.

passage.text: In 1945, an American engineer was working with a new kind of machine.
passage.reading: ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈfɔːrti ˈfaɪv, ən əˈmɛrɪkən ˌɛndʒɪˈnɪr wʌz ˈwɜːrkɪŋ wɪð ə ˈnuː ˈkaɪnd əv məˈʃiːn.

passage.text: Suddenly, he noticed that the chocolate in his jacket had melted.
passage.reading: ˈsʌdənli, hiː ˈnoʊtɪst ðæt ðə ˈtʃɔːklət ɪn hɪz ˈdʒækɪt hæd ˈmɛltɪd.

passage.text: He realized that the machine could heat food, and this led to the first microwave.
passage.reading: hiː ˈriːəlaɪzd ðæt ðə məˈʃiːn kʊd ˈhiːt ˈfuːd, ənd ðɪs ˈlɛd tə ðə ˈfɜːrst ˈmaɪkrəweɪv.

passage.text: In 1968, a scientist at an American company was trying to make a very sticky material.
passage.reading: ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈsɪksti ˈeɪt, ə ˈsaɪəntɪst ət ən əˈmɛrɪkən ˈkʌmpəni wʌz ˈtraɪɪŋ tə ˈmeɪk ə ˈvɛri ˈstɪki məˈtɪriəl.

passage.text: Instead, he made a material that was only a little sticky, and no one knew what to use it for.
passage.reading: ɪnˈstɛd, hiː ˈmeɪd ə məˈtɪriəl ðæt wʌz ˈoʊnli ə ˈlɪtəl ˈstɪki, ənd ˈnoʊ ˌwʌn ˈnuː ˈwʌt tə ˈjuːz ɪt ˈfɔːr.

passage.text: Years later, a colleague put it on the back of small notes, and the sticky note was born.
passage.reading: ˈjɪrz ˈleɪtər, ə ˈkɑːliːɡ ˈpʊt ɪt ɑːn ðə ˈbæk əv ˈsmɔːl ˈnoʊts, ənd ðə ˈstɪki ˌnoʊt wʌz ˈbɔːrn.

passage.text: Today, people around the world use millions of sticky notes every day.
passage.reading: təˈdeɪ, ˈpiːpəl əˈraʊnd ðə ˈwɜːrld ˈjuːz ˈmɪljənz əv ˈstɪki ˌnoʊts ˈɛvri ˈdeɪ.

passage.text: So the next time you make a mistake, don't worry too much.
passage.reading: soʊ ðə ˈnɛkst ˈtaɪm juː ˈmeɪk ə mɪˈsteɪk, ˈdoʊnt ˈwɜːri ˈtuː ˈmʌtʃ.

passage.text: It might be the start of something great!
passage.reading: ɪt maɪt bi ðə ˈstɑːrt əv ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈɡreɪt!
